- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is high (≥0.8) — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (≤0.3) — add 2–5% to forecast to account for potential rebound.
- Model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts — smooth 3–5 day moving average before forecasting.
- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over 3+ days, forecast should be slightly below historical mean of recent 10-day window.
- Overshoots in early forecast days (1–3) are common — apply downward correction of 3–8% for first 3 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion within 5–7 days after a spike, adjust forecast to reflect gradual decline — avoid sharp downward revisions.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- Forecast should not exceed 1.2x the 10-day moving average of recent history unless sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.9) and confirmed by 2+ consecutive days.
